doc.title: Jack DeJohnette interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 7, 2025

title: First compositions, titles and Malibu Reggae
summary: He writes from piano improvisations, sometimes starting with a title, such as Malibu Reggae for Directions' first ECM album.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Speaking of composition, I’m curious, can you recall one of the first compositions you wrote and did it come from an inspiration or just a curiosity to see if I can actually write something down?

Well you know I think I wrote improvising on the piano, so out of the improvisations would come compositions. Sometimes a composition was written because I had a title before I did the composition. So the composition, the title fit the outcome of the composition.
Could you give me an example of that? I think it’s interesting that you would have a title and then write around it. Can you recall one of your early tunes like that?

Let’s see. Early compositions. Well I wrote a composition when I had a group called Directions. And the first album we did on ECM I wrote a composition called “Malibu Reggae.” And to me it was a musical, trying to say portrait of Malibu, California. And so I added the genre of reggae to it. So it was kind of a playful piece, really.
Do you do that at the piano for the most part? Start your tunes at the piano?
Yeah most of the time I do but sometimes I just whistle a melody or get something from playing the drums or get a rhythm or groove or something like that.
